synopsis: The October 11 tutorial contributes an operational procedure for a small coding experiment: delegate instruction revision and repair attempts while retaining fixed grading and fresh-task evaluation. Its intended role in pieces 02 and 03 is methodological guidance about experiment design, trustworthy comparisons and budget planning. It does not establish measured performance improvement or model-weight training. The proposed outcomes and trial budget are illustrative, not observed results or spending. These orientation statements do not replace passage citations.
limitations_and_counterevidence: The supplied source contains no inspectable execution logs, actual instruction diffs, outcome tables or independent replication. Its candidate changes and outcome interpretations are prospective. It explicitly allows development gains to coexist with flat or worse held-out performance, and limits any favorable interpretation to the evaluated tasks. The planned 48 coding trials exclude optimizer work, setup and rehearsals; no actual monetary total is supplied. Automatic-transcript segment s00105 conflicts with adjacent fixed-attempt guidance and is deferred pending audio verification; it must not be treated as established advice to rerun until lucky. No independent verification was performed.

passages.purpose: Scope qualification: the underlying model stays unchanged, constraining interpretation of the title's self-training claim.
Method and delegation boundary: the optimizer changes workflow instructions while grading rules remain fixed.
Evidence-role qualification: proposed instruction changes are examples of candidates, not reported experimental results.
Reproducibility requirement: the tutorial calls for showing the instruction change and a trial transcript. This is a requested demonstration, not an inspectable artifact supplied here.
Comparison procedure: run each instruction version three times per task under the same limits; this segment also begins the advice to alternate run order.
Generalization limit and conditional counterevidence: rejects a universal coding upgrade and introduces the possibility that development improves while held-out results remain flat. Read with s00153.
Adjacent qualification: held-out results may worsen, in which case transferable improvement has not been demonstrated. This is a possible outcome, not an observed failure.
Planned experiment cost: states a total of 48 coding trials and begins the exclusion of additional overhead. Read with s00164; this is not a completed-run count.
Adjacent budget qualification: the trial count excludes the optimizer's own thinking, setup and rehearsals.
Cost uncertainty: reported dollar amounts should be treated as estimates with budget headroom, not exact expenditure guarantees.
